metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Italy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Italy using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA sampling design is complex (students nested in schools, with stratification and clustering), and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable names (e.g., student design weights) or whether replicate weights were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported means, percentages, correlations, and uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals) should be understood as accounting for PISA’s complex design, even though the specific weight variables and replicate method are not stated in this Italy factsheet.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking results rather than an empirical student-level modeling study that specifies how plausible values (PVs) and missing data were handled in an analysis pipeline. The outcomes reported here are descriptive and benchmarked (e.g., mean scores on a 60-point scale, proficiency level shares, and correlations) using OECD’s published PISA database outputs, but the factsheet does not document PV combination rules or missing-data procedures. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling details are not available from the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic subset reported for Italy includes 10,552 students in 345 schools who completed the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment (the factsheet notes that students in Italy completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 496,300 15-year-olds; the creative thinking results are presented for the PISA 2022 creative thinking test implemented in 64 countries/economies including Italy). No further inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., grade restrictions beyond PISA’s 15-year-old target, missing-response exclusions, or specific task-completion filters) are described in the provided factsheet text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III (Creative Minds, Creative Schools) Italy factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Italy performed on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test. The test measures the ability to generate, evaluate, and improve ideas, using 32 open-ended tasks across three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas; generating creative ideas; evaluating and improving ideas) and four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Italy’s mean creative thinking score is 31 on a 60-point scale, which is significantly below the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports proficiency shares (76% at least Level 3; 22% at Level 5 or 6) and relationships with mathematics and reading performance (correlations of 0.64 with mathematics and 0.62 with reading). It further highlights within-Italy gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and describes relative strengths/weaknesses across ideation processes and domain contexts, with uncertainty communicated via 95% confidence intervals. No machine-learning model training or PV/missing-data handling methodology is provided in this factsheet.
